paper: Rahman et al. (Spatiotemporal Graph Neural Networks for Groundwater Level Modeling)
main_difference_from_AquaSense: Relies on regular temporal discretization and graph adjacency; lacks explicit source reliability weighting and per-sample observability gating.

paper: Zhang & Sun (Multi-Source Deep Learning for Regional Groundwater Forecasting)
main_difference_from_AquaSense: Applies deep LSTM ensemble across gridded climate and well records; does not separate source reliability from observation gaps or test unseen-well spatial holdout.

paper: Li et al. (Physics-Informed Machine Learning for Regional Aquifer Dynamics)
main_difference_from_AquaSense: Integrates partial differential equations into loss function; does not provide quality-aware adaptive weighting for irregular historical well records.

paper: Wang et al. (Adaptive Attention-Based Multimodal Fusion for Hydrological Forecasting)
main_difference_from_AquaSense: Employs neural self-attention weights learned end-to-end; lacks explicit, interpretable data-quality dimensions (C, T, S, O) and causal annual weather leakage prevention.

paper: Mukherjee et al. (Robust Groundwater Level Estimation Under Incomplete Sensor Networks)
main_difference_from_AquaSense: Focuses on spatio-temporal matrix completion and kriging pre-interpolation; does not evaluate context-adaptive feature gating or separate warm vs cold start on unseen wells.

paper: Chen & Kumar (Explainable Machine Learning for Groundwater Drought Assessment)
main_difference_from_AquaSense: Applies TreeSHAP to tree ensembles on static plus meteorology features; does not incorporate observation history features, source reliability, or adaptive fusion.

paper: Al-Areeq et al. (Multimodal Ensemble Learning for Groundwater Level Fluctuation)
main_difference_from_AquaSense: Applies stacking ensemble on meteorological and pumping data; lacks dynamic row-level sample observability gating and treats missing records through simple mean imputation.

paper: Kumar et al. (Uncertainty-Aware Deep Learning for Regional Water Table Depth)
main_difference_from_AquaSense: Employs Monte Carlo dropout for epistemic uncertainty; does not quantify input source reliability or adapt modality contribution under irregular observation intervals.

Systematically decouples Source Reliability R_m from Context Observability A_{i,m}; enforces strict causal weather lag (Y-1); separates unseen warm vs cold start; evaluates controlled degradation modes.
